transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, uh… I guess I’m here because things at home have gotten really hard to manage. My in-laws moved into our house, and since then I’ve just been… keyed up all the time, and worn down at the same time, if that makes sense.

I mean, I manage artists—musicians, mostly—and usually I’m the guy who takes the call immediately, fixes the problem, keeps the contract from blowing up. I used to be good at that. But lately I’ve been avoiding calls I’d normally jump on, and I actually almost let a musician’s contract fall apart because I couldn’t think straight. And then at home I’m snapping at my wife, which… that’s not how I want to be. It’s just been a lot.
Have you been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of work and family stress?

I don’t know… “down” is hard to answer. I mean, I’m not walking around thinking, like, everything is meaningless or whatever. It’s more that I’m constantly preoccupied.

I used to enjoy catching a live set or talking through a new artist’s direction, and now when someone starts telling me about their mix or their tour routing, I kind of drift because I’m thinking about what’s happening at home. Sorry, that’s work again, I know. Outside of that… I haven’t really stopped liking things, I just don’t feel like I get much space to enjoy them lately.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you had days where you felt down or sad most of the day, nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d say “sad most of the day nearly every day.” It’s more like… I wake up and my head is already full, you know? Like there’s no quiet.

Sometimes I probably look miserable—my wife says I get this look like I’m somewhere else—but I don’t know if that’s sadness exactly. It’s not like I’m sitting there crying all day. It’s more… the house feels crowded, and then my mind goes to this whole list of things, and I get stuck there.
Have you found that activities you used to enjoy, like going to a live show or working with artists, don’t feel as rewarding or pleasurable lately?

I’m not sure I’d put it as they don’t feel pleasurable, exactly. Like, if I’m at a show and the band is good, I can still tell they’re good. I still care about the work.

It’s just… I’m not always fully there. I’ll be listening to a set and then suddenly I’m thinking about whether someone at home is annoyed about the thermostat, or if dinner turned into a whole thing, and then I’ve missed half a song. Which is ridiculous, because I’ve sat through thousands of sets and I’m usually locked in.

So I don’t know if the enjoyment is gone. It’s more like it gets interrupted, if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot more than usual, even when there isn’t anything specific happening, or feeling like you can’t control your thoughts?

Yeah… I mean, I think that’s basically why I’m here. Since my in-laws moved into our house, I’ve been so keyed up all the time. Even when nothing is actively happening, I’m sort of bracing for the next thing.

And then it spills everywhere. I’m snapping at my wife over stuff I’d normally just let go. I’ve been avoiding calls I would usually handle immediately—which is not like me, because in my business if you don’t call back, the whole thing starts sliding. Actually, there was this musician’s contract that almost fell apart because I just couldn’t think straight long enough to deal with it properly.

So, yeah, it’s not always one specific worry in the moment. It’s like my mind won’t shut up, and I’m worn down from it.
Have you noticed any physical changes, like feeling restless, being easily tired, or having trouble sleeping, even if you’re not actively stressed about something?

Yeah, I mean… “physical” is tricky, because I mostly notice it as being keyed up and worn down at the same time, if that makes sense. Since my in-laws moved into our house, I feel like I’m always bracing.

And then it shows up in stupid ways. I snap at my wife, I avoid calls I’d normally handle right away—and I’m usually very on top of that, because if you miss one call in this business, suddenly everyone’s calling everyone else and the whole thing becomes a mess. I almost let a musician’s contract fall apart because I just couldn’t think straight.

So… yeah. I don’t know if that answers the sleep or restlessness part exactly, but I’m definitely not operating like myself.
Over the past two weeks, have you had days where you felt down or sad most of the day, nearly every day?

I don’t know if I’d say “most of the day, nearly every day.” I mean, I’ve had bad days, sure, but it’s hard for me to separate “sad” from just… being fed up or distracted.

Like yesterday I was driving and this song came on that I used to book people around years ago, and I started thinking about how much simpler that whole period felt—but then five minutes later I was thinking about an email I forgot to answer. So it’s not like I’m sitting there crying all day or anything.

I guess I’m not sure I’d call it sadness in that steady way you’re asking.
